_README: docs/29 §5.2 — the signed-silence record. A key the glass detector cannot find in any
renderer is reported as a GLITCH until it appears here with a disposition AND a reason.
That is the whole mechanism: silence signed, never defaulted. Adding a line here is a
judgment you are putting your name to, not a way to quiet the tool.
Disposition is one of GLASS / EVIDENCE / REPORT / INTERNAL / DEAD / REPAIR (§5.2 + NUM-7). Reason answers
docs/29 §5.3 step 4 — 'does this already have a home, anywhere, live or archival?' — and
names that home. DEAD means the producer should be deleted; a DEAD entry that outlives
the session that wrote it is itself a defect.

NUM-7 (signed Rab 2026-08-31): `census_dispositions` (below, SEPARATE from this detector-validated dict) holds docs/51's numeration rows — they key on census ids no lane harvests, so they must never sit in `dispositions` (69 of them once did and armed a permanent stale-signature red on the close gate; review C1 2026-08-31). REPAIR = computed correctly, consumer broken — fix the wiring, then retire the entry. The 13 contested census rows are deliberately ABSENT until Rab signs them.

lanes.name: converter
lanes._note: The converter writes the manifest and the receipts. Its readers are downstream CODE rather than a surface, so a hit here means 'something consumes it', which is weaker than 'a human sees it' — the bench and widget lanes then re-check whether the consumer projects it onward. `manifest.chunking.seams[]` (docs/29 §7.3) is the case this two-hop shape is built to catch.

SCOPE NOTE, and it is the point of this entry: bench.py was NOT touched this session. This key entered the --since scope from `analyst.py`'s request body, which S79 edited for the residency fix, because the filter harvests key NAMES across the whole *.py diff and then attributes them to whichever lane has a producer using that name. That is the identical mis-scoping S79 diagnosed in the `bench:reason` entry below at 21:00 and then reproduced at its own close six hours later. docs/31 §5.2 item 7 — whether outbound request bodies are 'measured, stored values' at all — is UNSIGNED, and this is the second piece of evidence that they are not.
